title: (No AI) Twitch streamers can now opt out from training Amazon’s AI
author: Jay Peters
content:
![The Twitch logo against a pink and purple background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/STK044_VRG_Illo_N_Barclay_1_twitch.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Twitch users [can now opt out](https://x.com/TwitchSupport/status/2087572924450455558?s=20) of allowing their content to be used to train Amazon's generative AI models. Opting out means that "your streams, VODs, clips, stream chats, and pictures and text on your channel" won't be used in "future training" of an Amazon AI model "whose purpose is to generate or synthesize text, audio, images, or video," [according to a Twitch support page](https://help.twitch.tv/s/article/twitch-account-settings?language=en_US#FAQ).

Other "AI-supported" features like captions and safety tools will still function if you opt-out of generative AI training. However, if you participate in a chat on another person's stream, "their opt-out preferences govern if that chat can be used for training," Twitch …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/979112/twitch-streamers-can-now-opt-out-from-training-amazons-ai)

title: (No AI) Guitar company D’Addario admits that AI music was used in a promotional video
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![D’Addario logo imposed over image of a person playing guitar.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/1583922033086.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Maybe don’t let the AI shred next time. | Image: D’Addario

After weeks of controversy and speculation, music company D'Addario has [admitted](https://guitar.com/news/industry-news/daddario-admit-ai-controversy/) that AI, specifically Suno, was used as part of a recent promotional video. For nearly two weeks, the company has [denied the allegations](https://www.guitarworld.com/gear/guitar-strings/daddario-denies-using-ai-in-string-demo-video), even as evidence piled up against it. It offered various explanations, from low-quality exports, to combinations of plug-ins like Autotune introducing digital noise, and the use of AI-assisted mastering tools from LANDR and Logic. But now the company has edited its original Instagram post denying the use of generative AI to say it was wrong.

In a lengthy update to [its post from July 29th](https://www.instagram.com/daddarioandco/p/DbYvntjIOzg/) (embedded at the bottom), it said:

> …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/978982/daddario-guitar-ai-music-suno)
